title: fix(pm): make the rerun os-regen-merge prescribes able to perform step 2
body:
Fixes #18895

Clause-②: no

`scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` told the operator, on every conflict exit, to resolve and rerun
it "to redo the generated-artifact half", and there was no tree state in which that rerun could
perform step 2. The run that starts the merge now records the three shas it already reads before
step 1, and the rerun reads them back.

## Reproduced first — the card filed a reading, deliberately not a run

The card is explicit that the rerun was never executed and that a fix validated against its prose
would be validated against a reading. So the first thing built was a fixture harness that runs the
**unmodified** script (`origin/main`, md5 `2b146f4a8e7a68614d0893d081a1105d`) through the whole
operator sequence: run it, resolve the conflict, commit, rerun.

Each fixture is a real bare origin plus a clone with a driver registered, carrying **both halves of
one merge** — they pull step 2 in opposite directions:

- `gen/mixed.txt` — both sides move it, the driver text-merges it and it **CONFLICTS**, so the
  operator sees both sides and merges them by hand;
- `gen/deferred.txt` — both sides move it, the driver **DEFERS**: exit 0, keeps ours, says nothing.
  Main's side is gone, and nothing downstream reports it. Step 2 against the pre-merge base is the
  only thing that puts it back.

### OLD code, one fixture per conflict-exit branch

| branch taken | the exit's instruction | rerun, tree dirty | rerun, resolution committed |
|---|---|---|---|
| class 1 only (non-generated) | "then rerun this script" | exit 1, `working tree not clean` | **exit 0**, 0 sides taken, main's side still dropped |
| class 2 only (MIXED routed) | "then continue with step 4" | exit 1, `working tree not clean` | **exit 0**, 0 sides taken, main's side still dropped |
| class 1 + class 2 | "then rerun this script" | exit 1, `working tree not clean` | **exit 0**, 0 sides taken, main's side still dropped |
| class 3 (NOT_DRIVER_MANAGED) | "then rerun this script" | exit 1, `working tree not clean` | **exit 0**, 0 sides taken, main's side still dropped |

Verbatim, from the class-1+2 run on the old script:

```
[run 1] exit 1
[run 1] conflict headline: x merge stopped on conflicts in BOTH non-generated and generated files:
[run 1] says 'rerun this script': 1
[run 1] gen/silent.txt = silent v1-BRANCH   main's side present: 0
[leg A: rerun while the tree is dirty] exit 1 :: x working tree not clean - commit or drop local changes first
[leg B: commit the resolution, rerun on a clean tree] exit 0
[leg B] merge-base HEAD origin/main = d62ed07 ; origin/main = d62ed07
[leg B] 'TAKING main s side' notices: 0
[leg B] 'KEEPING the branch s bytes' notices: 2
[leg B] main's side restored in worktree: 0
[leg B] main's side restored in HEAD:     0
[control] by-hand step 2 against the pre-merge base d3055bd:
[control] gen/silent.txt = silent v1-MAIN
```

The control line is the whole point: the repair was **always available**, and only the base was
wrong. `merge-base HEAD origin/main` equals `origin/main` on that line — the card's mechanism,
observed.

### The two branches the card left unmeasured, and one it did not count

The card asked whether `:699` and `:737` reach the same dead end by the same route. **They do, and
the route is not a property of any branch**: every conflict exit returns the operator to the same
preamble, which refuses a dirty tree and derives a wrong base from a clean one. The branch only
decides which text prints before `exit 1`.

One correction to the card's count, measured: there are **four** conflict exits, not three, and the
fourth (class 2 only) did not say "rerun this script" at all — it said "continue with step 4". It
reaches the same place by **omitting** step 2 rather than by prescribing an inert one, which is
strictly quieter. All four now carry one shared instruction, emitted from one function.

### NEW code, the same four fixtures

```
[run 1] exit 1                                     (unchanged: step 1 still stops on the conflict)
[run 1] says 'rerun this script': 1                (all four branches, one shared text)
[leg A: rerun while the tree is dirty] exit 1      (unchanged: the dirty refusal still holds)
[leg B: commit the resolution, rerun] exit 0
[leg B] first line: -> RERUN: the merge committed in HEAD is the one this worktree recorded
[leg B] 'TAKING main s side' notices: 1            (the DEFERRED path, and only it)
[leg B] main's side restored in worktree: 1
[leg B] main's side restored in HEAD:     1
```

and the operator's hand resolution of the conflicted path survives:

```
gen/mixed.txt in HEAD: RESOLVED both intents
record: phase=done base=9596489... branch_tip=31872de... main_tip=f2b78b5...
second run: -> step 2 is already discharged for the merge in HEAD - nothing to merge and nothing to redo   (exit 0)
```

## What the record is, and what it is not

It is **not** the `--base` flag the header refuses. Nothing is supplied by the operator and nothing
is guessed: the run that starts the merge writes the base, its own pre-merge tip and the
`origin/main` tip it is about to merge into `$GIT_DIR/os-regen-merge-base`, and the rerun reads
them back. It is the same base, at the only moment it can still be read. A base it cannot read is
one it **refuses to invent**.

Three findings changed the shape the dispatch suggested, each measured:

1. **The rerun must not re-read `origin/main` at all.** The suggested detection asked whether
   `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` equals `origin/main`'s tip. In this repo `origin/main` is a
   **shared ref** a sibling's fetch advances, so between the conflict and the rerun it can move, and
   that test then answers "not a rerun" for a merge that plainly happened. Containment is asked
   against the **recorded** main tip instead, and step 2 restores from that pinned sha. A moved
   `origin/main` prints a notice and is not merged in — the rerun repairs the recorded merge only.
2. **A completed run marks its record `done` instead of deleting it.** "Leave nothing behind" and
   "refuse when no base is recorded" cannot both hold: a clean completion and a rerun nobody
   performed leave trees that read **identically** (clean, HEAD contains `origin/main`, step 2
   provably inert). Deleted, the refusal would fire on a finished merge. Marked, the settled tree
   reports "already discharged" and exits 0 exactly as it always did — pinned as a case.
3. **The conflict exit records which paths it left conflicted.** Without that, the rerun's step 2
   takes main's side of the MIXED path the operator just hand-merged — reverting the resolution the
   message asked for. A conflicted path is one git could **not** resolve silently, so no side was
   dropped there; step 2 chooses a side only where the driver chose one without saying so. Both
   directions are pinned, because a fixture with only one of these paths would pass with the other's
   rule deleted.

Refusals, all non-zero, all printing the record: a **missing** record in the rerun tree (and it
computes the by-hand step 2 from the merge commit's own two parents, which is what the PR 18752
round did by hand), a record whose branch tip is **not an ancestor** of HEAD, and a record naming a
commit this repository does not have.

```
x HEAD already contains origin/main and NO pre-merge base is recorded - refusing to run
  step 2 against a base that is knowably wrong.
  ...
  HEAD is a MERGE COMMIT, so both sides are still readable from it: ...
    base=$(git merge-base 9d58a6f5... cab1efd9...)
    git restore --source=cab1efd9... -- (every path in BOTH lists)   # tree only, never --staged
```

`scripts/regen-artifacts.mjs`, `scripts/git-merge-regen.mjs` and `scripts/check-regen-pending.mjs`
are read, never edited. The driver's `os-regen-pending` marker is theirs and is neither written nor
read here; the header says so. Both files live in `$GIT_DIR` for the same reason — in a linked
worktree that is `.git/worktrees/NAME`, so parallel agents never read each other's merge.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh --self-test`: **79 cases before, 122 after**, all pass, both
  measured in-tree (the baseline copy run out of tree fails case 9c on a relative ledger path, which
  is the harness, not the script). Case 10 drives the prescribed sequence end to end; case 10b is
  the **discriminating mutation** — neutralising the single `rr_mode="$(rr_classify)"` call site
  restores the old behaviour exactly, and the same fixture then reads exit 0, zero sides taken, and
  main's side still dropped in the commit. The card is reproducible on demand, in the tree, forever.
- Derived gate families: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`
  from this worktree, **23 commands, all exit 0**, each captured with redirect-then-`$?`.
  `--ran` reconciliation: `23 derived famil(ies) accounted for - 23 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED
  zero - all 23 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)`. The set includes
  `check:bash32-floor`, `check:self-test-wired`, `check:self-test-workflow-commands`,
  `check:scripts-symbol-anchors`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:parse-guard`, `check:nul-bytes`.
- No workspace package is touched, so there is no dependency-closure build and no package test or
  typecheck owed. No tracked test file names this script: its `--self-test` is its suite.
- `pnpm lint` narrowed, and the narrowing is a **measurement** rather than a skip, at `752a3abff`:
  the population read from `eslint.config.mjs` itself is
  `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}']` (plus narrower TS-only blocks); `--format json`
  over the one changed file returns 1 entry with 0 errors and the single message
  `File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied.` — i.e. **0 files linted**; and the
  config declares no `parserOptions.project` and no typed rules (its own comment at line 328 says
  so), so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.
- Control-character self-scan over the changed file: no match (`check:nul-bytes` green as well).
- `skip-changeset` measured rather than assumed: the root package is `private: true`, and across the
  76 published `packages/*` manifests, **0** `files[]` entries reach `scripts/pm`. Nothing publishes.

## Reader test

An operator who hits a class-2 conflict, resolves it, commits and reruns as the message says now
gets step 2 against the pre-merge base: main's dropped side is restored and committed, their own
resolution is left alone, and step 4's regeneration then re-derives the generated artifact on a
known-good base — carrying both sides, as PR 18752's round showed a correct step 2 buys.

## Acceptance notes

- The branch is 3 commits behind `origin/main` on four disjoint paths
  (`content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`, `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`,
  `packages/spec/scripts/check-duration-unit-keys.ts`, `scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs`),
  none of them this file, none generated, so the joint-breakage re-check is scoped to nothing and
  the merge was deliberately not taken. Re-deriving the gate families after a fresh fetch returns
  the identical 23 commands. Declared, not skipped.
- Step 2 was also fixed to restore from a **pinned sha** rather than the `origin/main` ref on the
  plain path too, since a sibling's fetch can advance that shared ref mid-run. The self-test's
  source-spelling pin moved with it: it now pins the non-staging verb against that variable and
  keeps both staging spellings as absences.
- **noted, not filed:** the `lint.yml` step comment describing this self-test says "five small
  fixture repos to pin 23 cases". That was already stale before this PR (the tree's own count was 79
  across nine fixture builders) and is now 122. It is prose in a workflow comment with no gate
  reading it, and no PR or person is routed to that file by this change — successor: none. Left as
  it is rather than widening this diff into `.github/workflows/`.
